name: Xanthan gum
aliases: E415, INS 415, xanthan gum, xanthan, goma xantana, goma xanthana, gomme xanthane
what_is: Xanthan gum (INS 415 / E415) is a high-molecular-weight polysaccharide produced by fermenting a carbohydrate source with Xanthomonas campestris. Codex lists it as a thickener, stabiliser, emulsifier and foaming agent.
why_botia: Xanthan gum is a polysaccharide made by fermentation. A very small amount can thicken a lot of liquid, which is why it appears in sauces, ice cream, gluten-free baking and plant drinks alike. It is largely not digested in the upper gut and can be broken down by intestinal bacteria; higher intakes can increase gas, while JECFA assigned an ADI “not specified”.
can_1: Detect E415, INS 415, xanthan gum and xanthan when explicitly declared on the label.
can_2: Explain its fermentation origin, texture functions, gastrointestinal behaviour and JECFA's ADI “not specified”.
cannot_1: Determine how much xanthan gum is present from the ingredient declaration alone.
cannot_2: Identify the exact carbohydrate used for fermentation or predict an individual's gastrointestinal response from the label.
